items.definition: A detailed plan of a journey, showing the places you will visit and when.
examples: Our itinerary includes two nights in Edinburgh and a day trip to the Highlands.

items.definition: The activity of visiting famous or interesting places as a tourist.
examples: We spent the first day sightseeing and the second one on the beach.

items.definition: To report your arrival at an airport or hotel and get your boarding pass or room key.
examples: You need to check in at least two hours before the flight.
We checked in at the hotel and went straight to the pool.
We set off at six in the morning to avoid the traffic.

items.definition: A period of time when something happens later than planned, for example a train or a flight.
examples: There was a two-hour delay because of fog.

items.definition: To get on a plane, ship, train or bus.
examples: Passengers are asked to board through gate twelve.

items.definition: A holiday in which the travel, the accommodation and often the meals are sold together at one price.
examples: We booked a package holiday to Crete because it was cheaper than arranging everything ourselves.

items.definition: A short stay in a place between two parts of a long journey.
examples: We had a ten-hour stopover in Dubai, so we left the airport and saw the city.
collocations: break the journey with a stopover

items.definition: In a place that is far from the usual tourist routes and therefore quiet and unspoilt.
examples: We stayed in a tiny village off the beaten track, where we hardly saw another tourist.
collocations: a hotel off the beaten track

items.definition: To go away on holiday or for a short break, especially to rest after working hard.
examples: I desperately need to get away for a few days.
They got away to the coast for the weekend.

items.definition: The tired, confused feeling you get after a long flight across several time zones.
examples: It took me three days to get over the jet lag after flying back from Mexico.

items.definition: A place where you can put up a tent or park a caravan, usually with toilets and showers.
examples: The campsite was next to a lake and cost very little.

trap.en: Camping is the activity of sleeping in a tent. The place where you do it is a campsite.
trap.es: «Vamos a un camping» es We're going to a campsite. Camping es la actividad: We're going camping.

items.definition: Having sold more tickets or rooms than are actually available.
examples: The flight was overbooked, so they offered me money to take a later one.

items.definition: A place where many people go for a holiday, usually with hotels, beaches or other facilities.
examples: Benidorm is a popular seaside resort with British tourists.

items.definition: A ticket that lets you travel to a place and come back again. In American English it is called a round-trip ticket.
examples: A return ticket to Leeds is cheaper if you travel after nine o'clock.
